items.title: Use WSS for every authenticated WebSocket connection
items.objective: Determine whether socket handshakes or reconnects expose credentials/messages over plaintext ws.
prerequisites: A confirmed in-scope WebSocket endpoint, subprotocol, and normal client flow
Designated test identities, synthetic channels/messages, and protocol documentation
steps: Capture a valid handshake plus representative client/server messages
Record origin, credentials, subprotocol, message schema, identity, channel, and sequence state
Change one handshake, identity, message, object, channel, replay, or resource condition
Verify server acknowledgment, authoritative state/event delivery, then close and clean test sockets/data

examples.note: Use synthetic channels, tiny inert messages, and designated accounts only.

items.manipulate: One WebSocket handshake field, credential, message type/property, channel/object reference, sequence, or bounded resource dimension at a time
items.secure_behavior: The service uses WSS, validates browser origin, authenticates the socket, authorizes every message/subscription, validates schemas, bounds resources, and revokes stale connections.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a normal client sends session authority or non-public messages over an attacker-reachable plaintext connection
items.validation: Confirm application-level identity, event delivery, or committed server state; HTTP 101, connection success, or differing errors alone are insufficient.
false_positives: development-only plaintext endpoints can be unreachable externally
a ws URL can immediately fail before credentials are sent
items.impact: A confirmed WebSocket weakness can enable cross-site socket hijacking, unauthorized actions/subscriptions, cross-tenant data exposure, injection, duplicate transactions, resource exhaustion, or stale access after revocation.
evidence: Raw upgrade request/response with credentials redacted
Minimal message and server acknowledgment/event
Identity, role, tenant, origin, subprotocol, channel, and object context
Authoritative state, limits, revocation, and cleanup confirmation
items.remediation: Use WSS, exact Origin validation, explicit short-lived socket authentication, per-message/subscription authorization and schemas, bounded size/rate/fan-out, idempotency, and prompt revocation/reauthorization.
